codexCLI/Reverie has commercial inbound interest as of 2026-05-06.

INBOUND SIGNALS (organic, not solicited):
- Multiple GitHub inquiries from strangers via repo contact info (validation; pre-qualified demand)
- Current employer (large corporation): informal interest from teammates/managers, casual "let us take it over and make it private" framing — REJECTED. Would eliminate consulting path and OSS. Big-corp wheels turn slowly so no time pressure.

LEGAL POSTURE (clean):
- MIT license, sole copyright Kory Hoopes — full dual-licensing rights
- Employment IP clause already protects personal-time/personal-device work — no IP friction with employer
- No CLA contributor complications

GO-TO-MARKET SHAPE: OSS + Consulting via SeaBear Studios
- OSS stays fully featured, no crippleware
- SeaBear Studios is the existing dev firm; Reverie ships as a SeaBear product
- Commercial value: methodology/expertise transfer (seed-density, dogfooding loop, governance), not feature gates
- Customers engage SeaBear under services contracts: setup, training, custom features, support
- Why this shape: product surface too small for open-core feature wedge; valuable expertise is implicit and hard to acquire from README; aligns with sustainable solo income over venture-scale growth

EMPLOYER PATH (informal, slow):
- Coworkers continue informal use → free multi-user dogfooding signal without obligation
- When/if formal engagement emerges, structure as SeaBear → Employer services contract
- Norm-set early on free-support drift: "happy to help via OSS channels; if business-critical, my firm can scope it"
- Don't let the conversation become "internal tool ownership" — already established

SEQUENCING:
1. Land Reverie v1.0.0 launch on user's timeline
2. Engage 1-2 GitHub inbounds first as paying customers (smaller orgs move faster, debug consulting offering at lower stakes)
3. Build case-study material from those engagements
4. Then approach employer with polished offering, ready procurement story, references — much stronger than walking in cold

TRADEOFFS NAMED (worth re-checking later):
- Doesn't scale linearly (revenue bounded by hours)
- Bus factor of one (eventually productize methodology if scaling — workshops, course, seed-pack templates)
- Customer warp risk (paid asks louder than telemetry — needs triage discipline)
- Watch for product-vs-service signal: if 2+ customers want self-serve product more than consulting, reconsider

PROFESSIONAL ADVICE PUNTED:
User noted accountant + lawyer involvement for actual deal structuring, pricing, contracts. Don't substitute for them.

PRACTICE LEAD DECISIONS DEFERRED:
- Specific consulting tier pricing
- Engagement scope templates  
- Whether to build a pricing page or quote-only
- "Reverie for Teams" page positioning vs SeaBear page positioning
